questions.stem: The first Asian and first Indian to win a Nobel Prize, awarded in 1913, was:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore — Nobel Prize in Literature 1913 for 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings). He was the first non-European laureate. C. V. Raman — Physics 1930 (Raman effect). Mother Teresa — Peace 1979. Amartya Sen — Economics 1998. Other India-born or naturalised winners: Har Gobind Khorana (Medicine 1968), S. Chandrasekhar (Physics 1983), V. S. Naipaul (Literature 2001), Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Chemistry 2009), Kailash Satyarthi (Peace 2014), Abhijit Banerjee (Economics 2019).

questions.stem: The only Indian to win the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for discovering the effect of light scattering by molecules was:
questions.explanation: Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the Raman effect — inelastic scattering of light by molecules. 28 February (the day of his announcement, 1928) is India's National Science Day. S. Chandrasekhar (Raman's nephew, a naturalised US citizen) won Physics 1983 for work on stellar structure. S. N. Bose gave his name to bosons but never received a Nobel. Homi Bhabha led India's atomic programme but was never a laureate either.

questions.stem: Mother Teresa was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in:
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa (born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu in Skopje, 1910) received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her work with the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata. She was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1980. Canonised as Saint Teresa of Calcutta by Pope Francis in 2016. Kailash Satyarthi (Peace 2014, with Malala) is the other Indian Peace laureate.

questions.stem: Match the Nobel laureate with the year they won. A. Amartya Sen. B. Abhijit Banerjee. C. Kailash Satyarthi. D. Venkatraman Ramakrishnan. List-II: 1. 1998, 2. 2019, 3. 2014, 4. 2009.
questions.explanation: Amartya Sen — Economics 1998 (welfare economics, social choice). Abhijit Banerjee — Economics 2019 (with Duflo and Kremer, for experimental approach to poverty). Kailash Satyarthi — Peace 2014 (with Malala Yousafzai, for children's rights). Venkatraman Ramakrishnan — Chemistry 2009 (ribosome structure).

questions.stem: V. S. Naipaul, who was awarded the 2001 Nobel Prize in Literature, was of:
questions.explanation: V. S. Naipaul (1932-2018) was born in Trinidad to a family of Indian (UP/Bihar) origin. He became British by naturalisation and wrote in English. Major works: 'A House for Mr Biswas', 'In a Free State' (Booker 1971), 'India: A Million Mutinies Now'. Salman Rushdie (Indian-British), Jhumpa Lahiri (Indian-American) and Kazuo Ishiguro (Japanese-British, 2017 Nobel) are sometimes confused with him.

questions.stem: The Nobel Prizes are awarded every year on which date, the death anniversary of Alfred Nobel?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel died on 10 December 1896. The Nobel awards are formally presented every year on 10 December in Stockholm (all prizes except Peace) and Oslo (Peace Prize). Nobel himself invented dynamite; the prizes were set up in his will. The Prize in Economic Sciences (in memory of Alfred Nobel) was added in 1969 by the Swedish central bank — strictly speaking it is not one of Nobel's own five prizes.

questions.stem: Har Gobind Khorana won the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his work on:
questions.explanation: Har Gobind Khorana (Indian-American) shared the 1968 Nobel with Robert Holley and Marshall Nirenberg for deciphering the genetic code — how DNA triplets (codons) specify the 20 amino acids of proteins. Blood groups were discovered by Karl Landsteiner (Nobel 1930). Antibiotics — Alexander Fleming et al. (Nobel 1945) for penicillin.
